deflation_cross_check.neither_is_the_gate: Both numbers are E[max], the DSR-style margin. The gate is P(max >= observed) over the whole simulated distribution, which is a different and stricter question -- Task 36 found `deflation_view` clearing its bar in both arms while the gate rejected both.
deflation_cross_check.note: The two routes assume different things about the null. The closed form assumes N draws from ONE null; `max_of_n` takes the maximum over N draws from N DIFFERENT nulls, because the conditional framing (Task 32) made the null per-candidate. Where the per-candidate nulls differ in location, the pooled mean sits below the candidates that actually drive the maximum, and the closed form's bar comes out too LOW -- the opposite of its direction on homogeneous input, which Task 42 measured as +0.017 to +0.036 high.

n_trials_provenance: read from the tier-2 campaign summary; N as runs/ledger.jsonl defines it -- every trial including crashes, global across datasets, written as the trials happen. Tier 3 displays and sanity-checks it and never recomputes a bar from it.
promotion_note: Tier 3 cannot promote. The verdict type has three members and none of them means approval; PASS means nothing was found to veto. An auditor that only removes candidates is safe with an uncharacterised error rate, and this one's has not been characterised.
